meaning: Every released local claim is preserved verbatim and mapped to its pinned source labels, proof notes and internal dependency IDs; no Lean implementation or source theorem certification is asserted.

claims.name: Three-way pair coverage excludes every nontrivial free split
claims.statement: In a proper free split choose exclusive x in A1 and y in A2. Closedness keeps each singleton closure inside its factor, excluding x in closure{y} and y in closure{x}. Freeness excludes any positive binary tuple on this cross pair in either orientation. This contradicts A02, proving irreducibility with arbitrary additional relation arities.

claims.name: Completed binary orbitals or named unary links give the stated cases
claims.statement: Complete positive binary pair coverage supplies disjunct(iii) of C01. If a unary graph orbital is represented only by its named function, its corresponding pair is unary-reachable; require positive binary coverage on every remaining pair. Totality is retained from the source statement.

claims.name: Closure of any displayed relation tuple is irreducible
claims.statement: For any positive displayed tuple, its actual unary-generated closure cannot freely decompose: some factor must contain that WHOLE tuple, hence all its generators and every defined unary iterate. It is then the whole closure, not proper. Repeated entries, an E loop and arbitrary positive relation arities are handled; nullary tuples have no typing coordinates.

claims.name: HE maps restrict to actual induced closed pieces
claims.statement: For closed D^-<=C^-, any intrinsically old irreducible S<=D^- is also an actual old irreducible induced substructure of C^-. The given old HE therefore embeds S. Thus its restriction to D^- is an old HE, even if D^- itself is reducible.

claims.name: Completed rigidity embeds each expanded irreducible old reduct
claims.statement: For expanded irreducible D<=C, A05 gives D in K*, hence D^- in K. C04 makes h restricted to this whole D^- an old HE into H. A04 makes it an embedding. Do NOT infer that forgetting E preserves irreducibility.

claims.name: The same restriction embeds the universal edge diagram
claims.statement: On D and H* the new relation is exactly inequality. C05 injectivity therefore preserves and reflects E_*, as well as all old data. Hence the same h embeds every expanded irreducible D.

claims.name: Every displayed E edge has a locally completed closed support
claims.statement: For a displayed E(x,y), including a possible loop, C03 makes closure{x,y} irreducible. A05 places that actual support in K*, excluding x=y because completed E is irreflexive. C05 embeds its old reduct, forcing h(x)!=h(y).

claims.name: The given vertex map preserves every displayed expanded tuple
claims.statement: C07 preserves all displayed E edges. All old relations and defined unary values were already preserved by the GIVEN old h in A05. Thus that same map is an expanded homomorphism; it was not replaced by a chosen global injection.

claims.name: Same-map universal-edge homomorphism-embedding export
claims.statement: C08 is global homomorphism preservation and C06 is embedding on every expanded irreducible piece. Together they prove the source same-map HE conclusion. Global injectivity on reducible sources does not follow.

claims.name: The two stated completed-rigidity sufficient conditions are correct
claims.statement: If every completed K member is irreducible, any HE whose source is that member embeds its whole source by definition. If every completed homomorphism is already an embedding, the conclusion also holds for its subclass of HE maps. These justify A04 when supplied; SAP by itself does not.

claims.name: Typed structures have a faithful one-sorted closed encoding
claims.statement: D04 is a bijective presentation of typed objects with their sort partition and domain/tuple restrictions. Actual induced embeddings, closed subsets and free decompositions are the SAME maps/diagrams in either presentation. No extra sort labels, ill-typed function values or tuples can be inserted into an encoded K member.

claims.name: Encoding preserves hereditary irreducible SAP class data
claims.statement: Every encoded substructure of a typed K member remains type-correct and corresponds to a typed closed substructure; thus heredity and irreducibility transfer. Encode a typed strong amalgam span to get the same intersection and embeddings. This supplies the exact class hypotheses for HN2.6/2.11.

claims.name: The full ordered ambient is irreducible
claims.statement: Any two distinct points of an R_all object are joined by one direction of its positive strict order. A proper free decomposition would have exclusive cross points with that missing cross tuple, impossible. This holds even for ill-typed ambient models; small/empty cases have no nontrivial split.

claims.name: HN2.19 gives the all-model ambient Ramsey input with exact conventions
claims.statement: Apply E01 to the ONE-SORTED encoded language without imposing type axioms on its ambient witnesses. Strict/nonstrict linear-order conventions transport via adding/removing the diagonal. Finite linearly ordered objects are rigid, so copies correspond to unique embeddings; the published copy-arrow yields the required embedding-arrow. The pinned Lean declaration still needs receiving representation/order bindings.

claims.name: Arbitrary orders give hereditary ordered SAP K
claims.statement: Closed substructures of ordered K members retain their old K diagrams and restricted linear orders. For a strong old amalgam, identify the whole common ordered base and shuffle the two factor orders in each base interval, including empty base. Place any extra host points afterwards without changing either factor order. All functions/domains remain old ones, so the embeddings stay induced.

claims.name: Adding order preserves old irreducibility
claims.statement: If a closed old irreducible D^- gained a nontrivial free split after adding its induced order, forgetting that relation would give the same old free split. Thus the induced expansion of every old irreducible is expanded irreducible. No converse is asserted.

claims.name: Forgetting an ordered completion gives an old HE completion
claims.statement: Each old irreducible piece remains expanded irreducible by C16, so an ordered HE embeds its old restriction there. Forgetting only order keeps the old homomorphism and all domain data, giving an old HE. The argument applies to any actual induced ordered substructure as well.

claims.name: Raw one-generated unary closures are irreducible before typing
claims.statement: In any raw one-sorted partial unary diagram, a free factor covering generator x contains all its already-defined unary iterates by actual closedness. It equals the whole U_x and cannot be proper. No K membership, sort correctness, totality or obstruction bound is used here.

claims.name: Local completed membership forces point and function typing
claims.statement: Conditionally, if EVERY expanded irreducible of a raw candidate is an actual encoded ordered K member, C18 applies to each U_x. Its actual inclusion therefore forces x to satisfy EXACTLY one sort predicate and every unary domain/value to obey the prescribed input/output sorts, including undefinedness off input sorts and totality on intended ones. No typed theorem is applied before this conclusion.

claims.name: Each displayed arbitrary-arity relation has an irreducible support
claims.statement: Apply C03 to the unary closure of ALL entries of each displayed positive relation tuple in the raw candidate, including repeats and any arity. One free factor must contain the entire tuple and hence the entire support. This does not rely on binary pair coverage.

claims.name: Local membership forces relation tuple typing too
claims.statement: Under the same conditional membership hypothesis as C19, each C20 support is an actual encoded ordered K member. Every displayed old relation tuple therefore has its prescribed input sort sequence. Unary sort predicates were already controlled by C19; nullary relations have no argument-typing restriction. The added order is global, not a typed old tuple symbol.

claims.name: The HN membership test makes a raw candidate a legitimate typed input
claims.statement: Combine C19/C21: a raw candidate with every expanded irreducible in encoded K^< has a proper sort partition, correctly typed unary domains/values and correctly typed old relations. Forgetting only order is therefore a typed source for the many-sorted obstruction premise. This proves the needed adapter in the LARGER ambient rather than assuming typed Ramsey inheritance.

claims.name: HN test(ii) puts every old irreducible reduct piece in K
claims.statement: Fix the A08 test candidate. C22 makes it typed. Any old irreducible D^- becomes expanded irreducible under C16, so test(ii) places that induced expansion in K^<. Forgetting order gives the ACTUAL D^- in K, exactly the restricted all-irreducible-admissible premise.

claims.name: Absence of an old completion produces a small actual closed obstruction
claims.statement: If C^- had no K HE completion, A07 applies by C23 and gives a noncompletable actual induced unary-closed D^- with |D^-|<=N. This uses the restricted supplied bound, not a theorem about arbitrary malformed unary diagrams.

claims.name: Restore its displayed order without changing size or closedness
claims.statement: Use the SAME point set and functions of D^- and the relation induced from the candidate C order. Since order is relational, D is an actual expanded induced substructure of C, still of size<=N<=n=max(1,N). No generated-closure size enlargement occurs.

claims.name: Small-test completion contradicts that obstruction
claims.statement: Test(iii) gives D a K^< completion. C17 forgets it to a K HE completion of D^-, contradicting C24. Therefore C^- HAS an old K completion. If N<0 the alleged nonnegative-size obstruction is already impossible; the same implication holds.

claims.name: HN2.6 supplies an INJECTIVE old homomorphism-embedding
claims.statement: Use E02 with the encoded hereditary irreducible unary SAP class from C12 and the old completion C26. Obtain f:C^-->B in K globally injective AND an old HE. This is a STRONG completion in HN terminology; it need not reflect missing old relations on the entire reducible source.

claims.name: The map to C0 excludes every displayed strict-order cycle
claims.statement: The A08(i) map preserves every displayed order edge into a strict linear order of C0. A directed closed walk, including a loop, would give a strict chain returning to its start, impossible. Global injectivity of this ambient map is not needed for acyclicity.

claims.name: The injective old completion transports this DAG without new cycles
claims.statement: Use the C27 injection to relabel all displayed order edges on its image in B. A directed cycle there would lift uniquely to a displayed cycle in C, excluded by C28. Noninjective relabelling would not justify this step.

claims.name: Extend the finite transported DAG to a total target order
claims.statement: Add the remaining B points as isolated vertices of the constraint DAG. Finite topological sorting supplies a strict total order extending every displayed comparison. Thus B^< is an allowed ordered completed K member and f preserves ALL displayed source order edges. Empty sets cause no exception.

claims.name: Each expanded irreducible piece has an old irreducible completed reduct
claims.statement: For any actual expanded irreducible D<=C, test(ii) gives D in K^<. Its old reduct belongs to K and is irreducible by the CLASS hypothesis A06, not by forgetting order in general. Its source order is already TOTAL.

claims.name: The injection reflects all old data and order on each protected piece
claims.statement: C27 old HE embeds D^- from C31. C30 preserves every source comparison; since D order is total and f injective, its restriction also reflects order (including false diagonals). Thus f restricted to D is an ordered induced embedding. No global old relation reflection is used.

claims.name: Assemble a STRONG ordered completion of the whole candidate
claims.statement: Old homomorphism preservation is C27, order preservation C30, and embedding on EVERY expanded irreducible is C32. Thus f:C->B^< is an ordered HE and is globally injective, providing a strong K^< completion.

claims.name: Uniform HN local finiteness in the larger ambient
claims.statement: For EVERY C0 in R_all and EVERY test candidate with cutoff max(1,N), C23-C33 produce a completion, stronger than Definition2.8 requires. The same cutoff works independently of C0. In particular local finiteness holds in the intended typed ambient as a restriction of this implication.

claims.name: HN2.11 turns the proved local finiteness into Ramsey
claims.statement: R_all is irreducible by C13 and Ramsey by C14; ordered K is hereditary with SAP by C15 and locally finite by C34. Apply E03 to get the ordered K Ramsey conclusion. Ordered rigidity transports the published copies convention to embeddings. No relational-closure-description2.18 theorem is substituted.

claims.name: Restricted irreducible-source HN theorem export
claims.statement: C34 proves the stated uniform local finiteness, indeed in a larger raw ambient, and C35 proves Ramsey using the THREE exact published inputs. No unary closure-size bound, completed-map rigidity for universal E, CCO or geometric obstruction theorem is assumed beyond the explicitly supplied A07 restricted bound.

claims.name: B034 converts actual irreducible membership to the direct domain
claims.statement: For a correctly typed partial source whose every old induced irreducible belongs to K, apply I01 selected C20/C21: each U_x is an ACTUAL completed K member and intended unary functions are already total. This is exactly one-generated admissibility, without optional m-bounds, hidden-specific interfaces or mere completable diagrams.

claims.name: The direct obstruction premise discharges the main restricted premise
claims.statement: For any source in the main A07 domain, C37 places it in the A09 one-generated-admissible domain. If noncompletable, A09 gives the SAME actual closed obstruction size<=N. Thus A07 is PROVED from A09 for this instance, not an additional independent hypothesis of the direct application.

claims.name: Direct unary HN transfer with exact conditional discharge
claims.statement: Instantiate the conditional main theorem C36 with the restricted bound supplied by C38 and the unchanged hereditary irreducible SAP class. It gives uniform max(1,N) local finiteness and Ramsey. Neither a universal-edge adapter nor binary pair coverage is required.

claims.name: The binary specialization supplies completed irreducibility
claims.statement: For every completed member under A10, positive binary coverage is disjunct(iii) of the C01 schema. Hence it is irreducible. This DISCHARGES that class hypothesis for the direct theorem; hereditary SAP and the restricted N-bound remain supplied. Retain the source arity<=2 scope although the coverage proof itself tolerates more arities.

claims.name: Binary-covered direct Ramsey transfer export
claims.statement: Apply C39 with irreducibility derived by C40 and the remaining actual direct premises. The same local-finiteness cutoff and Ramsey conclusion follow. Binary coverage has not supplied the N-bound, a homogeneous ambient, countability, CCO or exact geometry.

claims.name: No theorem here bounds arbitrary malformed unary sources
claims.statement: Local tests and direct obstruction premises require actual completed singleton diagrams (or the stronger all-irreducible membership), not mere unary closedness or totality. Malformed long unary cycles can fail that actual membership and are outside the bounded domain. No numerical size bound on singleton closures is used by this transfer.

claims.name: Without rigidity the same-map edge claim fails
claims.statement: In the empty old language K=all finite sets, the two-point constant map to a singleton is an old HE because old irreducibles are singletons. Expanding its source by a universal irreflexive edge makes all local pieces completed K*, yet that same constant map sends the edge to a forbidden diagonal. A different injection does not rescue the SAME-map assertion.

claims.name: Rigidity still allows global collapse and reducible old reducts
claims.statement: With K complete irreflexive R graphs, a two-isolated-point partial source may map constantly to a singleton and remain old/expanded HE, though K maps are rigid. Separately, two named sorts with at most one completed point each have rigid completed maps while their two-point old reduct is reducible; its universal-E expansion is irreducible. These show why C05 uses rigidity on a completed OLD HE restriction, not a false forgetting-irreducibility claim.

claims.name: Strong completion is not a global induced embedding
claims.statement: Two isolated points with no old R edges have an injective HE into a complete two-point irreflexive R graph: each irreducible singleton embeds and old positive tuples are preserved. The missing source R pair is added, so the whole map is not induced. Prop2.6 requires and supplies only the injection needed for C29.

claims.name: Binary coverage and singleton admissibility do not imply a uniform N
claims.statement: In completed equivalence-colored networks let R mean same-class distinct and B different-class. This complete binary class has SAP and irreducible members. An n>=4 partial R path with a B edge between its endpoints is noncompletable even homomorphically; every proper induced substructure completes by its R-components, while its irreducibles are completed edges/singletons. Thus admissibility/coverage alone allow unbounded minimal obstructions; the supplied N premise is substantive.

claims.name: Typing and exact closed tests remain explicit
claims.statement: Raw local candidates may have absent/multiple sort predicates, off-sort unary domains/values or wrong-sort relation tuples; C18-C22 reject them through actual irreducible membership. Definition2.8(iii) tests actual induced functional substructures, not arbitrary nonclosed weak relational subsets. These conventions and the three pending receiving Lean bindings must survive implementation.

claims.name: Every positive tuple has an irreducible distinct-entry support
claims.statement: In the induced structure on all distinct entries of a displayed tuple, a free amalgam must place that tuple wholly in one factor. That factor contains the entire vertex set, contradicting properness. This covers all finite relation arities and repeated entries; nullary truth never changes under the later map.

claims.name: HE irreducibles contain at most one point of a collision fibre
claims.statement: The current HE restricts injectively to each induced irreducible source piece. Thus such a piece cannot contain two distinct source vertices of F_v. In particular C01 controls the distinct-entry support of EVERY displayed positive tuple. No SAP or distinguished-family assumption is used.

claims.name: Distinguished factors also contain at most one fibre point
claims.statement: Injectivity of h on each S_i in A03 implies |S_i intersect F_v|<=1, independently of whether S_i is irreducible or whether h reflects its SOURCE relations. This is exactly the extra invariant needed for its image type.

claims.name: Use the full finite target image as an age object
claims.statement: B=h(A) with all induced U relations is finite and belongs to Age(U). It contains every current image point and all its higher-arity and negative atomic information. No completion of the partial source A is being asserted by naming this induced B.

claims.name: Deleting the collision value gives an actual relational base
claims.statement: Because there are NO functions, B minus {v} with its induced structure is an actual age subobject, including unary sorts and nullary truth. This deletion step would not automatically be closed in a functional language.

claims.name: SAP gives two copies differing outside the whole base
claims.statement: Strongly amalgamate two copies of B over the entire induced B minus {v}. Their off-base images of v are distinct and both are outside the shared base; their images intersect exactly there. The resulting finite age object may contain additional points, which do not affect the two induced copies.

claims.name: Embed the finite amalgam and align the first copy with old B
claims.statement: Embed the C06 age object into U. The first B-copy is induced-isomorphic to the literal old B; homogeneity extends that inverse identification to an automorphism of U. Apply it to the whole amalgam, fixing the first copy pointwise onto old B. The second v-image becomes vprime outside ALL old B by strong intersection.

claims.name: The second copy is a full induced replacement clone
claims.statement: After C07 alignment, the second B-copy supplies g_v from D05, identity on B minus {v} and sending v to vprime. It preserves and reflects every relation symbol in the whole signature, repeated-coordinate tuples, unary tags and nullary truth. Signature finiteness is unnecessary.

claims.name: Split one current fibre without changing any other source images
claims.statement: Choose a nonempty proper T subset F_v. Send T to vprime and keep F_v minus T at v; leave every other source image unchanged. Both sides are nonempty, and vprime was absent from h(A). Denote this new map h_T.

claims.name: The split is a GLOBAL positive homomorphism
claims.statement: For every displayed source tuple, C01/C02 say its distinct-entry support contains at most one F_v point. All occurrences of that one source point move together. Its image tuple is therefore unchanged or obtained by applying the full clone C08, which fixes every other image point. Positive relations of ALL arities are preserved; nullary truth is unchanged.

claims.name: The split still embeds every irreducible source piece
claims.statement: An irreducible source D has at most one F_v vertex by C02. Its new restriction is unchanged, or g_v composed with its old induced embedding. Both are induced embeddings in U. Together with C10 global positive preservation, h_T remains a HE.

claims.name: Every distinguished IMAGE type and its injectivity survive
claims.statement: By C03 each S_i sees at most one split-fibre vertex. Its new restriction is unchanged or its image is obtained through g_v. Thus it remains injective and h_T(S_i) is induced-isomorphic to old h(S_i), over the unchanged other points when applicable. This does not claim that h embedded the SOURCE S_i.

claims.name: The collision measure decreases by exactly t times r-minus-t
claims.statement: If the old fibre has size r and |T|=t with 0<t<r, its old choose(r,2) collisions become choose(t,2)+choose(r-t,2). Difference is t(r-t)>0. Other fibres are unchanged and vprime is new, so there are no new cross-fibre collisions. Image cardinality increases exactly one.

claims.name: Finite iteration yields an injective HE with all image invariants
claims.statement: Repeat C04-C13 while the current map has a collision. It remains a HE and every distinguished restriction stays injective, so all step hypotheses persist. The natural collision measure strictly decreases and terminates at zero. Compose the per-step image isomorphisms for each S_i to preserve its ORIGINAL induced image type.

claims.name: Relational collision-unfolding source export
claims.statement: C14 gives h-prime:A->U globally injective and HE, preserving the full induced type of EACH distinguished image separately. It uses homogeneous relational U with age SAP, not CCO, unary closure or a binary-language assumption. Neither global source inducedness, the joint distinguished-union type nor literal positions are asserted.

claims.name: Empty sources, already injective maps and arbitrary signatures
claims.statement: If mu(h)=0, including empty/singleton source cases, take h-prime=h immediately. Otherwise finite vertex images/induced isomorphisms suffice for each step even with infinitely many finite-arity relation symbols. Countability is retained from the source; the finite argument uses only age embeddability and homogeneity.

claims.name: Every fan triangle and shared complete edge is genuinely in K
claims.statement: Fix a simple m-cycle of complete A. Each actual triangle {v0,vi,v(i+1)} and each complete shared edge is an induced <=3-point A structure, so belongs to K by A07. Use their ACTUAL chord colours, not newly chosen representatives.

claims.name: Start with the first actual triangle and the partial fan invariant
claims.statement: The first triangle provides F_1 and its identity realization in a K host. At stage i retain ONLY the actual star and consecutive path edges in D09 and a homomorphism into some complete H_i in K. No constraint is placed on other pairs of formal fan vertices.

claims.name: The old fan map embeds the complete shared edge
claims.statement: For incoming T_i with i>=2, restrict the CURRENT F_(i-1) map to v0-vi. Its irreflexive atom forces distinct images. The complete/exclusive source and target edges have the same atom, converse and unary tags, so this restriction is an induced embedding.

claims.name: AP glues the next actual triangle over that pinned edge
claims.statement: Apply A05 to current host H_(i-1) and incoming T_i from C17, along the exact shared complete edge v0-vi from C19 and the triangle inclusion. Obtain a K amalgam and induced factor maps. Off-base vertices may be identified; this is AP, not SAP.

claims.name: Compose all old fan images and append the new triangle vertex
claims.statement: Compose the ENTIRE F_(i-1) map with the amalgam embedding and send v(i+1) through T_i. They agree at both base endpoints and give the next F_i map. Every old star/path edge survives; the new path edge/star chord and converses come from T_i. Nonadjacent old images may collide because unrecorded A chords impose no requirement.

claims.name: Induct finitely through the fan and recover the closing cycle edge
claims.statement: Starting with F_1, apply C19-C21 for i=2,...,m-2, obtaining final F_(m-2) on all cycle vertices. For m=3 no AP step is needed. The fan includes v0-v1, every consecutive cycle edge and the closing star edge v(m-1)-v0. Its restriction is a colour homomorphism of the whole cycle into a K host.

claims.name: Every specified simple cycle is homomorphically feasible
claims.statement: C17-C22 apply to ANY simple cycle of complete A. Different cycles may use different K hosts and nonadjacent collisions. This establishes only cycle feasibility; no global completion, CCO, SAP or triangle-fullness conclusion has yet been used.

claims.name: Semantic HOM CCO gives one whole-input homomorphism
claims.statement: The complete input has allowed unary/small diagrams by A07 and every specified simple cycle feasible by C23. Apply the supplied A06 implication to obtain ONE colour-preserving homomorphism h:A->H in K. Do not infer this solely from fan AP or triangle legality.

claims.name: Completeness and irreflexive diversity force global injectivity
claims.statement: For every distinct x,y in COMPLETE A, its specified diversity atom holds on that pair and is preserved by C24. Its target interpretation is irreflexive, so h(x)!=h(y). No SAP or separate collision-unfolding helper is used.

claims.name: Unique complete atoms give full induced reflection
claims.statement: If a target binary atom b holds on h(x),h(y), source distinct x,y have their unique atom a, which C24 preserves. Target exclusivity forces b=a, so reflection holds. Converse colours, logical equality/false diversity diagonals and complete exclusive unary tags also agree by C25 and the atomic code. Arbitrary extra predicates outside A04 are not covered.

claims.name: Heredity gives membership of the complete source A
claims.statement: C25/C26 make the colour map an induced embedding A->H in K. Its actual induced image belongs to K by heredity and A belongs by isomorphism closure. Thus complete local <=3 membership implies A in K.

claims.name: The at-most-three-point premise handles all small input cases
claims.statement: If |A|<=3, the premise already includes A itself. For larger A the fan proof applies to m>=3 cycles; realized unary tags and complete edges were also included. No empty path or unspecified chord needs an invented colour.

claims.name: AP plus semantic homomorphic CCO derives triangle fullness
claims.statement: Combine C27 for the fan/CCO argument and C28 for small inputs. This is a CONSEQUENCE for the selected hereditary atomic class, not an assumed FULL triangle class. The branch requires neither countability/homogeneity, SAP, unary functions nor the collision-unfolding theorem.

claims.name: AP without SAP does not guarantee relational collision unfolding
claims.statement: In a countable homogeneous matching graph the age has AP but not SAP. A partial three-point R-star folds onto an edge and is a HE on its irreducible edges/singletons, yet no injective star homomorphism exists into a degree-one matching. Alternatively use a singleton named sort plus an infinite other sort and two source points of the singleton sort. These delimit the SAP hypothesis, not the triangle branch.

claims.name: An injective HE can still fail global inducedness
claims.statement: Two isolated partial source points may inject into an edge in the countable random graph. The source irreducibles are singletons, so this is an injective HE even though the absent source edge is added. Distinguished singleton images cause no issue. Thus C15 is not a global source-embedding theorem.

claims.name: Separate distinguished image types do not determine their joint union
claims.statement: In an infinite pure set, map two source points constantly and distinguish their singleton factors separately. Each singleton image type survives an injective replacement, but their joint image changes from one point to two. Therefore joint-union type/literal positions cannot be included in the claimed invariant, nor can source reflection be inferred from mere distinguished injectivity.

claims.name: AP and legal triples without CCO do not imply fullness
claims.statement: The age of a one-colour complete three-point graph has AP. Every <=3-point part of K4 is legal and all its simple cycles are 3-colourable/homomorphically feasible; an AP fan C4 may collapse into K3. But K4 has no homomorphism into K3 and is absent from this age. Thus semantic CCO is a substantive input.

claims.name: Partial displayed-triangle legality is weaker than the input premise
claims.statement: The age of K2 has AP and semantic homomorphic CCO via bipartiteness. A PARTIAL C5 has no displayed triangles but no K2 completion. This refutes only a partial triangle-consistency overgeneralization, not A07: its partial induced triples are not complete K members. Actual complete-input chord colours are necessary for C17 fans.

claims.name: Deleting a target point need not be an actual functional base
claims.statement: For B={0,1} with F(0)=F(1)=1, deleting v=1 leaves a nonclosed set. Thus the specific C05 clone-over-deletion construction is PURELY relational. This is a proof-mechanism boundary, not a claim against independent unary injectivization theorems with their own assumptions.

claims.name: Unary closures are singleton unions, including the empty case
claims.statement: cl(T)=union_(t in T) cl({t}); every term follows one generator and identity includes it. No constant term contributes at empty T. Thus finite unions of closed sets are closed, and finite singleton closures imply finite closures of finite sets. Arbitrary relations do not change closure.

claims.name: Automorphisms commute with closure and stabilisers coincide
claims.statement: For every g in G, g tau(t)=tau(gt), so g cl(T)=cl(gT). Every g fixing T fixes all term values, and T subset cl(T); hence G_T=G_cl(T). The same argument holds for FULL Aut(H).

claims.name: Term closure is pointwise definable before any orbit hypothesis
claims.statement: Every unary term value over T is fixed by its full-Aut stabiliser, giving cl(T) subset dcl_H(T) subset acl_H(T). The analogous inclusions hold for any subgroup G. No homogeneity, real generators or orbit infinitude is needed.

claims.name: Fresh frame separation implies closed-base infinite orbits
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on fresh frames D04, fix finite closed A and u outside A. B=cl(A union {u}) is finite closed. Choose D with cl(D) intersect B=A. Thus u outside cl(D), A subset cl(D), and A04 gives infinite G_D.u. Since G_D<=G_A by term-fixing, G_A.u is infinite. This implication uses SAME-G A04 and real generation scope, no SAP/homogeneity.

claims.name: Closed-base infinite orbits imply fresh frames by one common move
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on D05, choose finite real D0 generating a cover of finite closed A by A03. S=cl(D0) minus A is finite; every G_A orbit of S is infinite. Apply I01 once to S and Z=B minus A, giving g in G_A with gS disjoint Z. Put D=gD0 subset R. Closure equivariance and g fixing A give A subset cl(D) and cl(D) intersect B=A. This direction does NOT need A04.

claims.name: Generic fresh-frame equivalence and all finite hidden bases
claims.statement: Under A01-A04, C04/C05 prove the stated equivalence. WHEN EITHER equivalent condition holds, for arbitrary finite T subset H, C02 identifies G_T with G_cl(T). Every closure point is fixed; every point outside has infinite orbit by the closed-base condition. Hence acl_G(T)=dcl_G(T)=cl(T), with no homogeneity/SAP needed.

claims.name: Full-Aut SAP does not imply an arbitrary subgroup orbit condition
claims.statement: SAP of Age(H) refers to full-Aut stabilisers through the separate homogeneous criterion. A proper subgroup may have finite off-closure orbits even in an infinite pure set with SAP (take the trivial subgroup). It fails A04, so does not refute C06; it guards against dropping that actual subgroup premise.

claims.name: The age and induced union use unary closed substructures
claims.statement: In the A05 setting, an induced substructure on a unary-closed subset of a finite age object is again in the age. A finite union of two actual closed sets in H is closed by C01; higher-arity relations may cross factors and are inherited from H without affecting closure. This is hereditary closed age, not only real-generated objects or a free relational union.

claims.name: Conditional SAP builds arbitrarily many disjoint off-base copies
claims.statement: IF Age(H) has SAP, fix finite closed A and u outside A; B=cl(A union {u}) is finite closed. Repeatedly strongly amalgamate n B-copies over ONE common A.
